# Forest, banteng, and partly hidden wire — v01

Mode: built-in image_gen, new generation. Use case: photorealistic-natural.

This is a generated conceptual habitat scene for the 11-02 PAWS teaching animation. It is not a research-site photograph and must not imply an observed animal, actual snare location, or rescue outcome.

## Structured prompt specification

The exact single-string prompt passed to the built-in tool is preserved in `forest-banteng-wire-exact-tool-prompt-v01.md`.

Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: one cinematic but natural documentary-style 16:9 landscape background for an educational animation. Output 1600 × 900 pixels if possible.

Primary request: an eye-level photograph-like view into dry dipterocarp forest in eastern Cambodia in natural daylight, grounding a story about a healthy wild banteng and the difficulty of spotting a hidden wire snare. This is a conceptual scene, not a documentary record of a real event.

Scene: open tropical dry dipterocarp woodland, varied slender and mature tree trunks, irregular natural spacing, sparse understory with scattered low dry grasses, a textured carpet of dry brown fallen leaves and earthy ground. The forest extends credibly into the distance. A faint, narrow, gently curving forest path is visible in the middle-right and recedes among the trees. Natural neutral daylight with soft dappled patches, believable depth, no dramatic fog, no staged golden-hour glow.

Animal: exactly one healthy adult banteng stands moderately distant in the middle-left, approximately x 0.27–0.42 and y 0.40–0.67 of the image. It is an identifiable wild Southeast Asian bovine: reddish-chestnut coat, white lower legs, white rump patch if visible, slim curved horns, smooth shoulder line. It is not a bison, buffalo, gaur, ox or domestic cow. Calm natural stance in three-quarter profile; all four legs are anatomically plausible. The animal is separate from and several metres behind the wire. It is not touching or caught in anything.

Critical foreground detail: in the lower-right foreground, approximately x 0.68–0.82 and y 0.70–0.86, show an existing thin dull grey metal wire loop lying low and partly concealed among dry leaves. The loop is elliptical in perspective, approximately 18 cm across relative to the surrounding leaves. It is a realistic thin wire, not a rope or thick cable. A small arc of wire and part of the trailing wire are exposed enough to be recognizable when the camera later zooms in; most of the loop blends subtly into leaf litter. The wire remains visible at close view but is easy to overlook in the wide scene. Do not draw an arrow, circle, glow, marker, or any emphasis around it. Do not show assembly, mechanism, bait, or installation details.

Composition: 16:9 wide landscape, eye-level camera, not an aerial or drone view. Preserve the healthy banteng at middle-left, the faint forest path at middle-right, and partly hidden wire at lower-right as three distinct readable locations. Keep all critical features within the central 85 percent of the frame so slight zooms and responsive crops are safe. Foreground leaf litter is detailed enough for a later zoom toward the wire. Natural photorealistic texture, realistic animal anatomy and scale, restrained contrast, no stylization.

Avoid: people, rangers, ranger group photos, hands, vehicles, buildings, tents, equipment, binoculars, cameras, collars, fences, blood, injury, dead animals, trapped animals, animal distress, additional animals, text, labels, logos, watermark, UI, maps, diagrams, arrows, neon colors, cartoon rendering, fantasy forest, overgrown rainforest.
